docs.title: Formulation in code
docs.text: The equations implemented in code/, with pointers to the source files. They are the generic counterparts of chapters 6–10. The state ordering and some modelling details differ on purpose from the production solver.

docs.title: Atmosphere and propulsion: src/model/atmosphere.cpp, aircraft.cpp
docs.text:
• Atmosphere. ISA troposphere: \(T=T_0-Lh\), \(p=p_0(T/T_0)^{g/RL}\), \(\rho=p/RT\).
  • Propulsion. A constant-power propeller. The shaft power lapses with altitude following Gagg–Ferrar, \(P_{max}(h)=P_{max,0}\,(1.132\,\sigma-0.132)\), and the available thrust is \(T_{max}=\eta_p P_{max}(h)/\max(V,V_{stall})\).

docs.title: Point mass (UF): src/model/point_mass.cpp
docs.text:
State and control:

\[x=[x_N,\,y_E,\,z_D,\,V,\,\gamma,\,\chi,\,\mu,\,m]^\top,\qquad u=[T,\,C_L,\,p_\mu]^\top\] \[ \begin{aligned} \dot x_N &= V\cos\gamma\cos\chi + w_N, &\dot y_E &= V\cos\gamma\sin\chi + w_E, &\dot z_D &= -V\sin\gamma + w_D,\\ \dot V &= \frac{T-D}{m}-g\sin\gamma, &\dot\gamma &= \frac{L\cos\mu}{mV}-\frac{g\cos\gamma}{V}, &\dot\chi &= \frac{L\sin\mu}{mV\cos\gamma},\\ \dot\mu &= p_\mu, &\dot m &= -\frac{\mathrm{sfc}}{3.6\times10^6}\,\frac{TV}{\eta_p} \end{aligned} \]

with \(L=\tfrac12\rho V^2 S C_L\), \(D=\tfrac12\rho V^2 S (C_{D0}+kC_L^2)\) and ρ(h) from the ISA. The lift coefficient is a control (time-scale separation). uf::jacobian returns ∂f/∂x and ∂f/∂u in closed form. It includes dρ/dh through the altitude dependence, which a finite-difference Jacobian only captures approximately.

docs.title: Rigid body (FC): src/model/rigid_body.cpp
docs.text:
\[x=[x_N,y_E,z_D,\,u,v,w,\,\phi,\theta,\psi,\,p,q,r,\,m]^\top,\qquad u=[T,\delta_e,\delta_a,\delta_r]^\top\]

Evaluation order at each call:

  1. Compute \(R_{nb}(\phi,\theta,\psi)\), remove the NED wind in body axes, and get \(V_a\), \(\alpha=\operatorname{atan2}(w_r,u_r)\), \(\beta=\arcsin(v_r/V_a)\).
  2. Coefficients from linear stability derivatives with non-dimensional rates \(\hat p=pb/2V_a\), \(\hat q=q\bar c/2V_a\), \(\hat r=rb/2V_a\): \(C_L=C_{L0}+C_{L\alpha}\alpha+C_{Lq}\hat q+C_{L\delta_e}\delta_e\), \(C_D=C_{D0}+kC_L^2\), and \(C_Y\), \(C_l\), \(C_m\), \(C_n\) in the same way.
  3. Rotate the wind-axis forces \([-D,\,Y,\,-L]\) to body axes, then add weight and thrust (along body x).
  4. Moments: aerodynamic, plus the thrust-line offset \((0,\;z_T T,\;0)\).
  5. Integrate:
  6. \(\dot{\mathbf v}_b = \mathbf F/m - \boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf v_b\)
  7. \(I\dot{\boldsymbol\omega}=\mathbf M-\boldsymbol\omega\times I\boldsymbol\omega\) (with \(I_{xz}\), solved in closed form)
  8. the Euler-angle kinematics and \(\dot{\mathbf r}_{NED}=R_{nb}\mathbf v_b\).

docs.title: Trapezoidal collocation: src/formulation/transcription.cpp
docs.text:
\[\Delta_k=\operatorname{diag}(s_x)^{-1}\Big[x_{k+1}-x_k-\tfrac{\Delta t}{2}\big(f(x_k,u_k)+f(x_{k+1},u_{k+1})\big)\Big],\qquad \Delta t=\frac{t_f}{N-1}\]

Jacobian blocks for interval k (row-scaled by \(s_x^{-1}\)):

w.r.t. block \(x_k\) \(-I-\tfrac{\Delta t}{2}A_k\) \(x_{k+1}\) \(I-\tfrac{\Delta t}{2}A_{k+1}\) \(u_k,\;u_{k+1}\) \(-\tfrac{\Delta t}{2}B_k,\;-\tfrac{\Delta t}{2}B_{k+1}\) \(t_f\) \(-\tfrac{1}{2(N-1)}\big(f_k+f_{k+1}\big)\)

Only structurally nonzero entries of \(A\) and \(B\) are stored. The tests verify the whole Jacobian against central differences, and check that the defect of a smooth reference trajectory shrinks like \(\Delta t^3\) (second-order global accuracy).

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
Boundary. The full initial state is fixed. At the end, position and heading are fixed.

Path (per node, \(h\le0\)):

name expression stall \(1-V/V_{stall}(h,m)\) power \(TV/(\eta_p P_{max}(h))-1\) v_ne \(V/V_{NE}-1\) load_max, load_min \(n/n_{max}-1\), \((n_{min}-n)/\max(1,\lvert n_{min}\rvert)\) altitude \((h_{min}-h)/h_{min}\) bank, bank_rate \(\mu^2/\phi_{max}^2-1\), \(p_\mu^2/p_{max}^2-1\) (smooth two-sided bounds) gamma_max, gamma_min flight-path-angle limits cl_max, thrust_min \(C_L/C_{L,max}-1\), \(-T/T_{ref}\) nfz:<id> (one per zone) \((m_j-d_j(x,y))/\max(m_j,25)\) if the zone's altitude band overlaps the mission's (start to end altitude), otherwise \(-1\); \(d_j\) = signed distance to the polygon, \(m_j\) = margin

The zone's activity is decided once per mission, the same rule the planner uses, rather than per node: a per-node switch would make the row discontinuous in altitude, which a gradient-based solver cannot handle.

docs.title: Cost: Bolza form with a time–fuel dial
docs.text:
\[J=(1-\alpha)\frac{t_f}{t_{ref}}+\alpha\,\frac{\sum_k \bar T_k\bar V_k\,\Delta t}{E_{ref}}+\frac{1}{N-1}\sum_k\Big[\beta_c\sum_j\Big(\frac{\Delta u_{j,k}}{s_{u_j}}\Big)^2+\beta_s\sum_{i\in\{\gamma,\mu\}}\Big(\frac{\Delta x_{i,k}}{s_{x_i}}\Big)^2\Big]\]
  • α = 0 gives minimum time and α = 1 minimum propulsive energy (a fuel proxy).
  • The β terms penalise control and attitude increments, the two families of 10. Cost function. Without them a minimum-fuel optimum is bang-bang: thrust flips between zero and its limit, and the aircraft follows a saw-tooth glide–climb profile.

costGradient is analytic, and the tests check it against finite differences.

docs.title: Initial guesses
docs.text:
• coldStartGuess: a straight line at constant speed with zero controls. This is the linear-interpolation guess against which the thesis benchmarks its warm start. Its defects are O(1).

  • trimmedLineGuess: the same geometry, but each node carries the UF trim controls for the local flight-path angle, and the mass history is integrated consistently. Its defects are at machine precision.

  • scenario::fly (UC-06): a trajectory flown in closed loop by a guidance law, then resampled on the collocation nodes. It satisfies the dynamics up to the discretisation error of the mesh.

Neither straight-line guess bends around obstacles or meets a terminal heading that differs from the bearing. With a level start, the straight climbing line also violates the initial flight-path angle; UC-04 reports this as a nonzero boundary residual. The warm start below handles those cases: a Hybrid A* path flown by the guidance laws, in the spirit of the thesis's Hybrid A* → inverse-dynamics chain.

docs.title: Design-scenario guidance: src/scenarios/scenario.cpp
docs.text:
Both models share one guidance law:

\[\gamma_{cmd}=\operatorname{sat}_{\gamma_{max}}\big(k_h(h_{cmd}-h)\big),\qquad \mu_{cmd}=\operatorname{sat}_{\mu_{max}}\big(k_\chi(\chi_{cmd}-\chi)\big)\]
  • UF (dynamic inversion). The point-mass equations are inverted for the controls:
  • \(C_L\) from \(L\cos\mu=m(V\dot\gamma_{des}+g\cos\gamma)\), with \(\dot\gamma_{des}=k_\gamma(\gamma_{cmd}-\gamma)\);
  • \(T=D+mg\sin\gamma+mk_V(V_{cmd}-V)\);
  • \(p_\mu=k_\mu(\mu_{cmd}-\mu)\).

Each control is clipped to \(C_{L,max}\), \(T_{max}\) and \(p_{max}\). - FC (autopilot around the wings-level trim). - Pitch: \(\theta_{cmd}=\alpha_{trim}+C_{L,trim}(n-1)/C_{L\alpha}+\gamma_{cmd}\), held with \(\delta_e=\delta_{e,trim}+k_\theta(\theta-\theta_{cmd})+k_q q\). - Roll: \(\delta_a=k_\phi(\mu_{cmd}-\phi)-k_p p\). - Turn coordination: \(\delta_r=-k_\beta\beta\). - Speed: thrust from the trim value plus climb and speed terms.

The guidance is deliberately simple. Its purpose is to produce realistic, flyable reference trajectories for the design scenarios, not to be optimal.

docs.title: Missions with no-fly zones: src/model/environment.cpp, src/planning/planner.cpp
docs.text:
No-fly zones. A zone is a simple polygon in the horizontal plane, extruded between \(h_{min}\) and \(h_{max}\), with a margin \(m\). Its signed distance \(d(x,y)\) is the distance to the nearest edge: positive outside, negative inside (crossing-number test). A zone only counts for a flight whose altitude band overlaps \([h_{min},h_{max}]\), so a low zone can be overflown.

Dubins paths. Between two poses \((x,y,\psi)\), the shortest forward path with turn radius \(R\) is one of six words: LSL, LSR, RSL, RSR, RLR, LRL. Each word is computed in closed form, and the tests check that every word ends exactly at the goal pose.

Hybrid A*. The search runs over \((x,y,\psi)\) cells (20 m, 5°).

  • Edges. Five 30 m primitives with curvature \(\{-1,-\tfrac12,0,\tfrac12,1\}/R\), so every path is flyable at the planning radius \(R=V^2/(g\tan(0.8\,\mu_{max}))\). The 0.8 leaves bank for the guidance to correct errors.
  • Cost. Length, plus a small penalty for curvature and for changes of steering.
  • Heuristic. \(\max(\text{Euclidean},\ \text{Dubins length})\). Both are admissible lower bounds, so the maximum is too.
  • Collisions. Points every 5 m must keep \(d\ge m+\) safety from every active zone.
  • Analytic expansion. Every few expansions, and whenever the goal is within \(4R\), a Dubins shot to the goal is tried. If it is collision-free it closes the search.
  • Waypoints. The mission is planned leg by leg. Each waypoint's heading points to the next target.

L1 path following. The guidance finds the nearest point of the path, searching forward only so that loops are not skipped, and aims at a point \(L_1=2.5\,V\) further along. With \(\eta\) the angle between the course and the line to that point, the commanded lateral acceleration and bank are

\[a_{cmd}=\frac{2V^2}{L_1}\sin\eta,\qquad \mu_{cmd}=\operatorname{sat}_{\mu_{max}}\big(\arctan(a_{cmd}/g)\big).\]

The same command drives the UF model (through \(p_\mu\)) and the FC autopilot (through \(\delta_a\)). Altitude is handled by the guidance law of the previous section.

docs.title: Optimal-control problems: src/formulation/ocp_*.cpp
docs.text:
CollocationProblem turns a collocated model into a complete nonlinear program. Its constraint vector, with \(g_l\le g(z)\le g_u\), is

\[g(z)=\big[\;\Delta\;(=0)\;\big|\;\text{boundary}\;(=0)\;\big|\;h(x_k,u_k)\;(\le0)\;\big|\;\text{waypoints}\;(\le0)\;\big].\]
  • Boundary. The whole initial state is fixed: position, speed, flight-path angle 0, heading, wings level and mass m₀ for UF; the wings-level 6-DoF trim at the start for FC. At the end, the position and the heading (UF) or yaw (FC) are fixed, the angle matched modulo 2π.
  • Waypoints. Each waypoint is pinned to the node of the initial guess nearest to it, visiting them in order, and that node must lie within the tolerance: \(\big((x_k-x_w)^2+(y_k-y_w)^2\big)/r_w^2-1\le0\). This is simpler than the thesis's arc-length slack formulation. The price is that the share of flight time before each waypoint follows the guess.
  • Bounds. Boxes keep every function defined (airspeed above 0.3 V_cruise, pitch within ±60° away from the Euler singularity, mass between m_empty and m₀). FC actuator deflections are bounded at their real limits. The other limits are path rows.
  • Jacobian. The defect block comes from trapezoidalJacobian. UF supplies its analytic model Jacobians; FC supplies central differences of fc::rhs, scaled per variable, with the structural sparsity detected once. The path rows of node k depend only on \((x_k,u_k)\), so each node contributes a dense \(n_c\times(n_x+n_u)\) block, filled by central differences. Boundary and waypoint rows are analytic. The tests compare the whole Jacobian with a dense central-difference one.
  • References. Variable scales, the cost's \(t_{ref}\) and \(E_{ref}\) and the bounds on \(t_f\) come from the mission: the length \(L_{ref}\) of the polyline start → waypoints → goal and \(L_{ref}/V\). Cold and warm starts therefore solve the same problem.

FC path rows (\(h\le0\), normalised): stall and V_NE on the air-relative speed, power, incidence limits, sideslip \(\beta^2/\beta_{max}^2-1\), load factor \(qSC_L/(mg)\), altitude, bank, pitch limits, the three body rates, thrust sign, and one nfz:<id> row per zone.

The sideslip row is needed because the linear model's polar \(C_D=C_{D0}+kC_L^2\) has no sideslip drag. Without the row, the minimum-fuel FC optimum flies 15–27° sideways with the rudder saturated, and banks so that the side force \(C_{Y\beta}\beta\) carries part of the weight at no drag cost. It then appears to burn 6–9 % less fuel than the point mass, which is impossible for the same aircraft. With \(\beta_{max}=1°\) (coordinated flight), UF and FC agree to 0.2 %.

FC cost. \(J=(1-\alpha)\,t_f/t_{ref}+\alpha\,(m_0-m_{N-1})/m_{ref}\) plus the smoothness terms on \(\Delta T,\Delta\delta_{e,a,r}\) and \(\Delta\phi,\Delta\theta\). Fuel is read from the mass state, which integrates \(\dot m=-c\,T V_a\), the same quantity as the UF energy integral up to the factor \(c\). Its reference is \(m_{ref}=c\,E_{ref}\), so UF and FC costs are on the same scale.

No-fly zones between nodes. The zone rows hold at the nodes. A chord of length ℓ whose two ends keep distance r from a zone corner stays at least \(\sqrt{r^2-\ell^2/4}\) from it. The pipeline therefore enforces \(r=\sqrt{m^2+(\ell/2)^2}\), with ℓ the node spacing of a path 50 % longer than \(L_{ref}\), and the whole straight segment between nodes stays outside the real margin m. UC-08 checks this along the segments.

docs.title: UF → FC projection: src/warmstart/warm_start.cpp
docs.text:
ws::ufToFc maps a point-mass trajectory to rigid-body states and controls, node by node:

  1. Incidence and elevator. For each thrust, lift and pitch-moment balance are linear in \((\alpha,\delta_e)\): \(C_{L\alpha}\alpha+C_{L\delta_e}\delta_e=C_L-C_{L0}-C_{Lq}\hat q-T\sin\alpha/(qS)\) and \(C_{m\alpha}\alpha+C_{m\delta_e}\delta_e=-(C_{m0}+C_{mq}\hat q+z_TT/(qS\bar c))\). The thrust is \(T_{UF}/\cos\alpha\), because the point mass pushes along the velocity and the rigid body along its x axis. Three fixed-point passes on α converge.
  2. Attitude. \(R_{nb}=R_{nw}(\mu,\gamma,\chi)\,R_{wb}(\alpha)\) with zero sideslip; the Euler angles are extracted from \(R_{nb}\), and ψ is unwrapped next to χ.
  3. Rates. \(p,q,r\) come from the time derivatives of the Euler angles (central differences).
  4. Velocity. \((V\cos\alpha,0,V\sin\alpha)\) plus the wind in body axes.
  5. Aileron and rudder. They zero the roll and yaw moments at zero sideslip (a 2 × 2 solve).

On a trimmed straight line, the projection reproduces the 6-DoF trim to five digits (θ, δ_e, w), with a residual pitch acceleration of about 10⁻¹⁶ rad/s²; a test checks this.

docs.title: Sequence: src/pipeline/pipeline.cpp
docs.text:
pipeline::run executes, for one mission:

  1. Warm start (ws::build): Hybrid A* path; UF and FC runs flown by the guidance.
  2. UF stage. The UF run is resampled on N nodes (or a straight line, for a cold start), the problem is built with the mission references, and IPOPT solves it.
  3. FC stage. It is seeded by the projected UF optimum, or, without a UF stage, by the run flown by the FC autopilot. Then IPOPT solves it.
  4. Verification. nlp::verify checks each optimum against every constraint and bound. The stage records its status, iterations, time, objective, the defect of its initial point, and the share of the cost due to smoothing.

docs.title: Use cases: input reference
docs.text:
Every use case is a JSON file in code/data/cases/ with a use_case field and an aircraft path. Run them from code/:

./build/ofc data/cases/uc01_aircraft_report.json [more cases ...]

Paths are relative to the working directory. The program exits with a non-zero code if a case fails (for example, a trim that does not converge). Results and their interpretation are on the Worked examples page. For a step-by-step introduction to the input files, with every key of the optimisation cases explained, see the User guide, chapter 3.

docs.title: UC-01: Aircraft report
docs.text:
{ "use_case": "UC-01", "aircraft": "data/aircraft/generic_uav.json", "altitudes_m": [0, 1000, 2000] }

The report prints the input data and the derived performance: CL_max, k, (L/D)max, and a table over altitude with ρ, V_stall, the speed for best L/D, available power, and the thrust available at V_cruise. Use it to sanity-check a new aircraft file before anything else.

docs.title: UC-02: Trim
docs.text:
{ "use_case": "UC-02", "aircraft": "...", "flight": { "V_mps": 25, "h_m": 300, "gamma_deg": 0, "mu_deg": 0 } }
  • UF. Closed form: \(L\cos\mu=mg\cos\gamma\) and \(T=D+mg\sin\gamma\). The report also checks the trim against C_L,max, available thrust, n_max and the bank limit.
  • FC. Newton iterations on (α, δ_e, T) that zero u̇, ẇ and q̇ in straight, wings-level flight. The starting point comes from the UF trim and the linear lift and moment model.

docs.title: UC-03: Open-loop simulation
docs.text:
{ "use_case": "UC-03", "aircraft": "...", "flight": { "V_mps": 25, "h_m": 300 },
  "duration_s": 60, "dt_s": 0.01,
  "uf": { "bank_cmd_deg": 30, "bank_gain": 1.0 },
  "fc": { "elevator_doublet_deg": 2, "doublet_start_s": 2, "doublet_width_s": 0.5 },
  "output": "output/uc03" }
  • UF. Rolls into a coordinated turn following the quasi-steady schedule (\(C_L=C_{L,level}/\cos\mu\), T = D).
  • FC. Starts from trim with the controls frozen, plus an elevator doublet.

Outputs: uf.csv and fc.csv.

docs.title: UC-04: Transcription check
docs.text:
{ "use_case": "UC-04", "aircraft": "...",
  "mission": { "start_ned_m": [0, 0, -300], "end_ned_m": [3000, 800, -400], "speed_mps": 25,
               "gamma_start_deg": 0, "heading_end_deg": 15, "wind_ned_mps": [0, 0, 0],
               "alpha": 1.0, "beta_control": 0.01 },
  "N": [25, 50, 100, 200], "output": "output/uc04" }

gamma_start_deg and heading_end_deg are optional. For each N, the report gives:

  • the NLP size and sparsity;
  • the maximum normalised defect of a cold start and of a trimmed straight line;
  • the time per defect Jacobian, analytic against forward differences, and the relative error between them.

After the table it gives the cost, the boundary residual, a check of the cost gradient, and the worst value of every path constraint. Outputs: transcription_check.csv and sparsity_N<smallest>.csv.

docs.title: UC-05: Design charts
docs.text:
{ "use_case": "UC-05", "aircraft": "...", "altitudes_m": [0, 1000, 2000, 4000],
  "trim_altitude_m": 300, "turn_speeds_mps": [18, 25, 32], "mass_kg": 11.0, "output": "output/uc05" }
Output Content power_curves.csv thrust power required and available against airspeed, at each altitude envelope.csv V_stall, min-power speed, best-L/D speed, max level speed and max climb rate, every 250 m up to the absolute ceiling trim_curves.csv 6-DoF trim (α, δ_e, T) and UF trim thrust against airspeed turn.csv level-turn load factor, radius, rate and power against bank, at each speed

mass_kg is optional and defaults to m₀. The report prints the service ceiling (where the climb rate drops to 0.5 m/s), the absolute ceiling, and the envelope table.

docs.title: UC-06: Typical design scenarios
docs.text:
{ "use_case": "UC-06", "aircraft": "...", "nodes": 60,
  "speed_sweep_mps": [18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28, 30, 32, 34, 36],
  "scenarios": [
    { "id": "SC-03", "title": "Climb +200 m and 180 deg turn",
      "h0_m": 300, "climb_m": 200, "turn_deg": 180, "turn_start_m": 800, "distance_m": 2500,
      "V_mps": 25, "bank_deg": 30, "gamma_deg": 7.5 } ],
  "output": "output/uc06" }

V_mps, bank_deg and gamma_deg are optional. They default to V_cruise, ¾ φ_max and ½ γ_max.

Each scenario is flown by both models with the same guidance (see Formulation in code). For each one, the report gives:

  • flight time and fuel for UF and FC;
  • the largest UF–FC distance at the same along-track position;
  • the FC altitude error at the end, and the maximum FC bank;
  • the collocation defect of the flown UF trajectory on N and 4N nodes;
  • the path constraint closest to its limit;
  • the speed that uses the least fuel in the sweep.

Outputs per scenario: <id>_uf.csv, <id>_fc.csv and <id>_speed_trade.csv, plus a summary.csv for all of them.

docs.title: UC-07: Missions with no-fly zones and waypoints
docs.text:
{ "use_case": "UC-07", "aircraft": "...", "nodes": 80,
  "planner": { "cell_m": 20, "heading_bins": 72, "step_m": 30, "bank_fraction": 0.8, "safety_m": 10 },
  "missions": [
    { "id": "M-04", "title": "NFZ, waypoint, climb; low NFZ overflown",
      "h0_m": 300, "climb_m": 150, "V_mps": 25, "bank_deg": 30,
      "start": [0, 0], "start_heading_deg": 0, "end": [3300, 1500], "end_heading_deg": 90,
      "nfz": [ { "id": "A", "polygon": [[1500, 300], [2200, 300], [2200, 1150], [1500, 1150]],
                 "h_min_m": 0, "h_max_m": 1500, "margin_m": 40 } ],
      "waypoints": [ { "id": "WP1", "position": [2700, 900], "tolerance_m": 40 } ] } ],
  "output": "output/uc07" }
  • Coordinates. Positions are [north, east] in metres, and headings are in degrees from north towards east.
  • Polygons. Each polygon is a simple polygon, in any orientation.
  • Altitude band. A zone whose band does not overlap the flight's altitudes (h0_m to h0_m + climb_m) is ignored, that is, overflown.
  • Planner settings. planner sets the search grid, the primitive length, the fraction of the bank limit used for the planning radius, and an extra safety distance on top of each zone's margin.

For each mission the report gives:

  • the planner time, the turn radius and the planned length;
  • flight times for UF and FC;
  • the smallest distance to an active zone beyond its margin (≥ 0 is acceptable);
  • the largest waypoint miss distance;
  • the collocation defect on N and 4N nodes;
  • the worst NFZ row of the NLP for the flown trajectory and for a straight-line cold start (≤ 0 satisfied).

The program exits with code 2 if a path is not found or a check fails. Outputs per mission: <id>_path.csv, <id>_uf.csv, <id>_fc.csv, <id>_nfz.csv and <id>_points.csv, plus a summary.csv.

docs.title: UC-08: Optimal missions (needs IPOPT)
docs.text:
{ "use_case": "UC-08", "aircraft": "...",
  "pipeline": {
    "seed": "warm", "stages": "UF>FC", "fc_from_uf": true,
    "nodes_uf": 60, "nodes_fc": 60,
    "alpha": 1.0, "beta_control": 1.0, "beta_state": 1.0, "sideslip_max_deg": 1.0, "verify_tol": 1e-4,
    "planner": { "cell_m": 20, "heading_bins": 72, "step_m": 30, "bank_fraction": 0.8, "safety_m": 10 },
    "solver": { "tol": 1e-6, "acceptable_tol": 1e-4, "max_iter": 1500, "max_cpu_time_s": 120, "print_level": 0 } },
  "missions": [ ... same format as UC-07 ... ],
  "output": "output/uc08" }
Key Meaning Default seed warm (Hybrid A* path flown by the guidance) or cold (straight line) warm stages UF>FC, UF or FC UF>FC fc_from_uf seed FC with the projected UF optimum; otherwise with the run flown by the FC autopilot true nodes_uf, nodes_fc collocation nodes of each stage 60 alpha 0 = minimum time, 1 = minimum fuel 1 beta_control, beta_state smoothness weights on control and attitude increments 1, 1 sideslip_max_deg sideslip limit of the FC problem (coordinated flight) 1 verify_tol tolerance of the post-solve verification (rows are normalised) 1e-4 solver IPOPT options: tol, acceptable_tol, constr_viol_tol, max_iter, max_cpu_time_s, print_level, mu_strategy, lbfgs_history, linear_solver, derivative_test as shown

For each mission the report gives:

  • the warm-start time;
  • for each stage: IPOPT status, iterations, solve time, flight time, fuel and the share of the cost due to smoothing;
  • the smallest clearance beyond any zone's margin along the optimal paths (segments between nodes included);
  • the largest waypoint miss;
  • the local integration error of the UF optimum.

A stage that does not succeed (IPOPT did not converge, or it converged but the verification failed) is marked with !, and IPOPT's return code and the worst violated row of each group are printed below the row. Without IPOPT the case prints a notice and exits with code 0. Outputs per mission: <id>_ws.csv (warm start on the UF nodes), <id>_uf.csv, <id>_fc.csv, <id>_path.csv, <id>_nfz.csv and <id>_points.csv, plus summary.csv and report.json (every stage's status, IPOPT return code, seed, iterations, time, objective, initial defect, penalty share and verification summary).

docs.title: UC-09: Warm-start benchmark (needs IPOPT)
docs.text:
{ "use_case": "UC-09", "aircraft": "...",
  "pipelines": ["COLD>UF", "WS>UF", "WS>FC", "WS>UF>FC"], "repeats": 1,
  "pipeline": { ... as UC-08, seed and stages are set by each label ... },
  "missions": [ ... ], "output": "output/uc09" }

Each label is a seed (WS or COLD) followed by the stages. Every pipeline solves exactly the same problems: scales, cost references and t_f bounds come from the mission, never from the seed (only the node each waypoint is pinned to follows the initial point). With repeats > 1 the fastest run is kept. Outputs: benchmark.csv and benchmark.json.

docs.title: User guide
docs.text:
This guide explains how to install, run and understand the public implementation in code/. It is written to be read in order: each chapter assumes the previous ones and refers back to them where needed. Readers who only want to run an optimisation can stop after chapter 5; chapters 6 to 8 explain what happens inside the solver.

The guide covers the public code only. The thesis chapters (Problem, Theory, Results) describe the original solver and the research behind it, and are referenced where they add depth.

docs.text: Chapter Content You will be able to 1. Input files Case file, aircraft file, mission, pipeline, planner and solver settings; units and frames Write a valid case file for your own mission and aircraft 4. Reading the results Console table, CSV and JSON files, verification report, figures, exit codes Decide whether a run succeeded and where the numbers come from 5. The optimisation process Warm start, point-mass stage, projection, 6-DoF stage, verification; what each stage passes on Understand the pipeline and choose seeds, stages and node counts 7. Mathematical formulation Models, constraints, bounds, boundary conditions, cost, collocation, scaling, problem size Relate every row and variable of the NLP to its equation and source file 8. Using IPOPT Interior-point method, the adapter, every solver option, the iteration log, return codes, tuning Read an IPOPT log, diagnose a failed solve and tune the solver 9. Example catalogue Every bundled case file: purpose, key inputs, what to look at, where the results are discussed Pick the example closest to your problem and adapt it 10. Troubleshooting Build, input, planner and solver failures, with their remedies Recover from the most common errors 11. Using and extending the library C++ API, building a problem by hand, adding new constraints Call the optimiser from your own code or add a new constraint type

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need a C++17 compiler, CMake 3.14 or newer and, for the optimisation itself, the IPOPT solver. Python 3 with numpy and matplotlib is only needed for the figures. Chapter 1 gives the exact commands for each operating system.

No prior knowledge of IPOPT is assumed. Some familiarity with flight mechanics (lift, drag, bank angle, flight-path angle) and with the idea of constrained optimisation helps from chapter 6 onwards.

docs.title: Conventions used in the guide
docs.text:
• Commands are run from the code/ folder unless stated otherwise. Paths inside case files are relative to the folder the program is started from.
  • Commands are shown for Linux, macOS and Git Bash. On Windows PowerShell, the executable is .\build\Release\ofc.exe instead of ./build/ofc.
  • Numbers quoted from runs (iterations, times, fuel) were produced with the files in the repository. Iteration counts depend on the IPOPT version and its linear solver, and times depend on the machine, so expect small differences on your system.
  • Two model names appear throughout: UF is the point-mass model (8 states, 3 controls) and FC is the rigid-body, six-degree-of-freedom model (13 states, 4 controls).

docs.title: Where the rest of the documentation fits
docs.text:
If you need Read The background of the problem and the thesis results Problem and requirements, Warm-start benchmark, Conclusions The theory behind collocation, constraints and cost OCP and NLP to Warm start The code's module structure Architecture Every field of the aircraft file Aircraft file format The input keys of use cases UC-01 to UC-07 Use cases: input reference The results of every bundled example, with figures Worked examples

docs.title: 1. Installation
docs.text: This chapter builds the ofc program and its tests, with or without the IPOPT optimiser, and shows how to confirm which of the two you have.

docs.title: 1.1 What is needed
docs.text:
Component Version Needed for C++ compiler C++17 with <filesystem> (GCC ≥ 9, Clang ≥ 9, MSVC 2019 or newer) Everything CMake ≥ 3.14 Everything IPOPT 3.11 or newer (tested with 3.11.9 on Linux and 3.14.20 on Windows) Use cases UC-08 and UC-09, and the optimisation tests pkg-config any Finding IPOPT on Linux and macOS Python 3 with numpy and matplotlib any recent The figures only

The only bundled third-party code is nlohmann/json (a header-only JSON library, MIT licence) in code/third_party/. IPOPT is linked, never bundled.

IPOPT is optional at build time. Without it, the program builds, the tests run, and use cases UC-01 to UC-07 work; UC-08 and UC-09 print a notice and are skipped. Every other part of this guide that runs an optimisation needs IPOPT.

docs.title: 1.2 Get the code
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/pablourioste/uavtraj-opt.git
cd uavtraj-opt/code

All later commands are run from this code/ folder.

docs.title: Linux and WSL (Ubuntu, Debian)
docs.text:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install build-essential cmake coinor-libipopt-dev pkg-config

The distribution package provides IPOPT with the MUMPS linear solver. CMake finds it through pkg-config.

docs.title: macOS (Homebrew)
docs.text: brew install cmake ipopt pkg-config

docs.title: Windows (PowerShell)
docs.text:
Install Visual Studio 2022 or newer with the "Desktop development with C++" workload, and CMake (included with Visual Studio, or from cmake.org). Then, from code/:

.\utils\install_ipopt.ps1

The script downloads the official COIN-OR binaries (IPOPT 3.14.20, built with MSVC) into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Ipopt-3.14.20, checks the expected files, and sets the user environment variable IPOPT_DIR to that folder. Another version can be requested with .\utils\install_ipopt.ps1 -Version 3.14.x. Terminals opened before the script ran do not see IPOPT_DIR; run.ps1 reads it from the user environment anyway.

If PowerShell refuses to run scripts, allow local scripts for the current user once:

Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned

docs.title: Other systems
docs.text:
Any IPOPT installation works if CMake can find it in one of two ways:

  1. through pkg-config (the module is called ipopt), or
  2. through a folder that contains include/coin-or/IpTNLP.hpp (or include/coin/), the library in lib/ and, on Windows, the DLLs in bin/. Pass it as -DIPOPT_DIR=<folder> or as the environment variable IPOPT_DIR.

docs.title: 1.4 Build
docs.text:
The scripts configure, build and test in one step:

bash run.sh -t        # Linux, macOS, Git Bash

.\run.ps1 -t          # Windows PowerShell

Without -t, the scripts also run every bundled use case and plot the results (chapter 2).

The equivalent manual commands are:

cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --config Release
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure -C Release

On Windows with the prebuilt IPOPT, the build must use the Visual Studio generator, because the IPOPT binaries are built with MSVC:

cmake -S . -B build -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64
cmake --build build --config Release

run.ps1 selects this generator automatically when IPOPT_DIR is set, and resets the CMake cache if build/ was configured earlier with another generator. With the prebuilt IPOPT, CMake also copies the IPOPT DLLs next to ofc.exe and ofc_tests.exe after each build, so no change to PATH is needed.

docs.title: Build products
docs.text: File Content build/ofc (Windows: build\Release\ofc.exe) The command-line program build/ofc_tests (Windows: build\Release\ofc_tests.exe) The unit tests, run by ctest build/libofc_core.a (Windows: ofc_core.lib) The library with everything except main.cpp, for use in your own programs (chapter 11)

docs.title: CMake options
docs.text:
Option Values Default Effect OFC_IPOPT AUTO, ON, OFF AUTO AUTO links IPOPT if it is found; ON stops the configuration with an error if it is not; OFF never links it IPOPT_DIR folder environment variable IPOPT_DIR Prebuilt IPOPT, used when pkg-config does not find one OFC_BUILD_TESTS ON, OFF ON Build ofc_tests CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release, Debug, ... Release Optimisation level of single-configuration generators

Use -DOFC_IPOPT=ON whenever the optimiser is required: a build that silently lacks IPOPT is otherwise easy to miss.

docs.title: 1.5 Check the installation
docs.text:
During configuration, CMake reports what it found. One of these three lines appears:

-- IPOPT 3.11.9: trajectory optimisation enabled                     (pkg-config)
-- IPOPT from C:/Users/.../Ipopt-3.14.20-win64-msvs2022-md: trajectory optimisation enabled
-- IPOPT not found: building without the optimiser (use cases UC-08/09 will be skipped)

After the build, the program states it directly:

./build/ofc --info

ofc 0.2.0
optimiser: IPOPT (UC-08 and UC-09 available)

A build without IPOPT prints optimiser: not built (UC-08 and UC-09 are skipped; see code/README.md) instead.

The tests check the models, the analytic derivatives against finite differences, the planner, the warm start and, when IPOPT is present, complete optimisations. A successful run ends with:

100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 1

(ctest reports one test because all checks run inside a single executable; the individual checks are printed with --output-on-failure only when one fails.)

docs.title: 1.6 Figures and documentation (optional)
docs.text:
pip install numpy matplotlib          # figures: utils/plot_results.py
pip install mkdocs-material           # this documentation as a local website
mkdocs serve                          # run from the repository root, then open http://127.0.0.1:8000

docs.title: 1.7 Code formatting (contributors only)
docs.text:
The C++ sources follow code/.clang-format (clang-format 18, four-space indentation, 120 columns), and the continuous integration rejects unformatted code:

pip install clang-format==18.1.8
clang-format -i include/ofc/*.hpp src/*.cpp src/*/*.cpp tests/*.cpp tests/*.hpp

If the build or the IPOPT detection fails, see 10. Troubleshooting.

docs.title: 2. First run
docs.text: This chapter runs the bundled examples, explains the command line, and shows where the results are written.

docs.title: 2.1 Run everything
docs.text:
bash run.sh           # Linux, macOS, Git Bash

.\run.ps1             # Windows PowerShell

The script builds the program, runs the tests, runs the nine bundled case files data/cases/uc01_*.json to uc09_*.json in order, and finally calls utils/plot_results.py if Python is available. UC-01 to UC-07 finish in a second or two. UC-08 and UC-09 call IPOPT many times and take most of the run: between a few tens of seconds and a couple of minutes, depending on the machine.

At the end, a timing summary lists each case. This one is from a Windows laptop with IPOPT 3.14.20:

== Summary ==
    0.00 s  data/cases/uc01_aircraft_report.json
    0.01 s  data/cases/uc02_trim.json
    0.11 s  data/cases/uc03_simulation.json
    0.34 s  data/cases/uc04_transcription.json
    0.02 s  data/cases/uc05_design_charts.json
    0.31 s  data/cases/uc06_design_scenarios.json
    1.34 s  data/cases/uc07_nfz_missions.json
   23.02 s  data/cases/uc08_optimal_missions.json
   68.68 s  data/cases/uc09_warmstart_benchmark.json

docs.title: 2.2 The command line
docs.text:
ofc <case.json> [<case.json> ...]     run each case file in turn
ofc --info                            version, and whether the optimiser is built in
ofc --help                            usage

A case file is a JSON file that names its use case, its aircraft, its settings and its output folder (chapter 3). The program runs the case files in the order given. A case that fails does not stop the others; the exit code reports the worst outcome (section 4.6).

Run a single case (output shortened):

./build/ofc data/cases/uc01_aircraft_report.json

== UC-01  Aircraft report ==
name     : generic_uav
mass     : m0 11.00 kg, empty 8.50 kg, fuel 2.50 kg
geometry : S 0.550 m2, b 2.896 m, c 0.190 m, AR 15.24
aero     : CL_max 1.405, k 0.0550, (L/D)max 12.31 at CL 0.739

   h [m]        rho    V_stall    V_(L/D)  P_max [W] T_max@Vc [N]
       0     1.2250      15.10      20.82        800         22.4
     500     1.1673      15.47      21.33        757         21.2
     ...
min turn radius at V_cruise, phi_max: 76.0 m

Run the optimal missions:

./build/ofc data/cases/uc08_optimal_missions.json

Always start the program from code/. The paths inside the bundled case files (data/aircraft/generic_uav.json, output/uc08) are relative to the current folder. Started from elsewhere, the program stops with cannot open aircraft file: data/aircraft/generic_uav.json.

docs.title: 2.3 The bundled use cases
docs.text:
Use case Case file What it does Needs IPOPT UC-01 uc01_aircraft_report.json Prints the aircraft data and its derived performance UC-02 uc02_trim.json Steady-flight trim with both models UC-03 uc03_simulation.json Open-loop simulation: a coordinated turn (UF) and an elevator doublet (FC) UC-04 uc04_transcription.json Size, sparsity and derivatives of the collocated problem UC-05 uc05_design_charts.json Power curves, flight envelope, trim curves, turn performance UC-06 uc06_design_scenarios.json Four reference manoeuvres flown by guidance laws with both models UC-07 uc07_nfz_missions.json Hybrid A* paths around no-fly zones and through waypoints, flown by both models UC-08 uc08_optimal_missions.json Optimal missions: warm start, point-mass optimum, 6-DoF optimum ✓ UC-09 uc09_warmstart_benchmark.json The same missions solved by several pipelines, for comparison ✓ Tutorial tutorial_first_mission.json Three missions of increasing difficulty, used in chapter 5 ✓

UC-01 to UC-07 check the aircraft, the models and the warm start. UC-08 is the optimiser itself, and most of this guide is about it. Chapter 9 describes every example in detail.

docs.title: 2.4 Where the results go
docs.text:
Each case file has an output key, a folder relative to the current directory. The folder is created if it does not exist, and files from an earlier run are overwritten.

code/output/
├── uc03/ ... uc07/        CSV files of the simulations, charts and flown missions
├── uc08/                  per mission: <id>_ws.csv, <id>_uf.csv, <id>_fc.csv,
│                          <id>_path.csv, <id>_nfz.csv, <id>_points.csv;
│                          for the whole case: summary.csv and report.json
├── uc09/                  benchmark.csv, benchmark.json
└── figures/               PNG figures written by utils/plot_results.py

UC-01 and UC-02 print their results only. code/output/ is listed in .gitignore, so nothing in it is committed. Chapter 4 describes every output file.

docs.title: 2.5 Figures
docs.text:
python utils/plot_results.py                           # every use case found in output/ → output/figures/
python utils/plot_results.py --optimal output/tutorial # one folder written by a UC-08 case
python utils/plot_results.py --out ../docs/assets/figures/code   # refresh the figures of this documentation

Without arguments, the script reads the fixed folders output/uc03 to output/uc09 and skips those that do not exist. For UC-08 it plots the missions whose identifier starts with M-. Use --optimal <folder> to plot the results of your own UC-08 case file, whatever its mission identifiers; the figures are then named after the folder, for example tutorial_cover.png and tutorial_T-01.png.

docs.title: 2.6 What to try next
docs.text:
• Read the UC-08 table printed on the console and compare it with Worked examples: UC-08.
  • Open output/figures/uc08_cover.png and uc08_M-04.png.
  • Run the same case with "print_level": 5 in its solver block to watch IPOPT iterate (chapter 8).

docs.title: 3. Input files
docs.text:
An optimisation is described by two JSON files: a case file, which holds the missions and every setting of the run, and an aircraft file, which holds the design data of the aircraft. This chapter documents both for the optimisation use case (UC-08) and the benchmark (UC-09). The keys of the other use cases are listed in Use cases: input reference.

flowchart LR
    C["case file<br/>use_case, pipeline, missions, output"] -->|aircraft path| A["aircraft file<br/>mass, geometry, aero, envelope ..."]
    C --> P[ofc]
    A --> P
    P --> O["output folder<br/>CSV, JSON"]

docs.title: 3.1 Conventions
docs.text:
Topic Convention Units SI: metres, seconds, kilograms, newtons, watts Angles Degrees in every input key, and those keys end in _deg or _dps (degrees per second). Radians inside the code Horizontal position Local flat-Earth frame, in metres, written [north, east] Heading Degrees clockwise from north: 0 = north, 90 = east, 180 = south, -90 or 270 = west Altitude Metres, positive up. The code uses north-east-down (NED) axes internally, so its z is -h Paths to files Relative to the folder the program is started from (normally code/) Comments // and /* */ comments are accepted in case files. Aircraft files must be strict JSON Missing keys Optional keys take the documented default. Unknown keys are ignored, so a misspelt key silently falls back to its default: check the spelling when a setting seems to have no effect

The flight takes place in still air: UC-08 and UC-09 have no wind input.

docs.title: 3.2 The case file
docs.text:
A UC-08 case file has five top-level keys:

{
  "use_case": "UC-08",
  "aircraft": "data/aircraft/generic_uav.json",
  "pipeline": { ... },
  "missions": [ { ... }, { ... } ],
  "output": "output/my_case"
}
Key Required Meaning use_case ✓ "UC-08" for optimal missions, "UC-09" for the benchmark aircraft ✓ Path of the aircraft file pipeline Seed, stages, cost weights, node counts, planner and solver settings (section 3.4). Every key has a default missions ✓ List of missions (section 3.3). Each one is solved independently with the same settings output Output folder. Default output/uc08 (UC-08) or output/uc09 (UC-09)

The smallest valid case file uses every default: a 25 m/s cruise at 300 m from the origin, heading north, to a point 3 km north, minimising fuel.

{
  "use_case": "UC-08",
  "aircraft": "data/aircraft/generic_uav.json",
  "missions": [ { "id": "M-00", "end": [3000, 0] } ],
  "output": "output/minimal"
}

docs.title: 3.3 Missions
docs.text: Each element of missions describes one flight from a start pose to a goal pose. The same description feeds the planner, the guidance laws and both optimal-control problems.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Key Unit Default Meaning id text "SC" Identifier, used in the console table and in the output file names. Give each mission a unique one title text id Free description, written to report.json h0_m m 300 Initial altitude climb_m m 0 Altitude change. Final altitude = h0_m + climb_m; negative values describe a descent V_mps m/s aircraft V_cruise Initial airspeed (a fixed boundary condition) and commanded speed of the warm start bank_deg deg ¾ of phi_max_deg Bank angle used by the warm start: it sets the planner's turn radius and limits the guidance gamma_deg deg ½ of gamma_max_deg Largest flight-path angle the guidance uses to climb or descend start m [0, 0] Start position [north, east] start_heading_deg deg 0 Initial heading end m required Goal position [north, east] end_heading_deg deg 0 Final heading nfz none List of no-fly zones (below) waypoints none List of waypoints, visited in the order given (below)

docs.title: What is fixed and what is free
docs.text:
The optimiser does not choose the start or the goal; it chooses everything in between, including the flight time.

Quantity At the start At the end Position and altitude Fixed: start, h0_m Fixed: end, h0_m + climb_m Heading Fixed: start_heading_deg Fixed: end_heading_deg (any multiple of 360° is accepted) Airspeed Fixed: V_mps Free Flight-path angle, bank Fixed: level, wings level Free Mass Fixed: take-off mass m0_kg Free (it is what minimum fuel maximises) 6-DoF attitude, rates, controls Fixed: wings-level trim at V_mps and h0_m Free

bank_deg and gamma_deg only shape the warm start. The optimiser itself is limited by the aircraft envelope (phi_max_deg, gamma_min_deg, gamma_max_deg), so the optimum may bank or climb more steeply than the warm start did.

docs.title: No-fly zones
docs.text:
"nfz": [
  { "id": "TOWN", "polygon": [[1200, -400], [2000, -400], [2000, 500], [1200, 500]],
    "h_min_m": 0, "h_max_m": 1500, "margin_m": 40 }
]
Key Unit Default Meaning id text "NFZ" Name, used in the constraint labels (nfz:TOWN) polygon m required At least three vertices [north, east], in either orientation. The polygon must be simple: its edges may not cross h_min_m, h_max_m m 0, 10⁹ Altitude band of the zone; h_max_m must be greater than h_min_m margin_m m 0 Required horizontal distance from the polygon

A zone is a vertical prism: the polygon extruded from h_min_m to h_max_m. It is active for a mission if its band overlaps the altitudes the mission spans, from h0_m to h0_m + climb_m. An inactive zone is ignored everywhere, so the aircraft may fly over it (see mission M-04 in UC-08). The decision is taken once per mission, not per node, because a constraint that switches on and off with altitude would be discontinuous.

Three distances are involved, from the inside out:

  1. margin_m, the distance the trajectory must keep. The verification checks it along the whole optimal path.
  2. The margin the optimiser enforces at the nodes, slightly larger so that the straight segments between nodes also keep margin_m (section 7.5).
  3. margin_m + safety_m (planner setting, default 10 m), the distance the warm-start path keeps.

docs.title: Waypoints
docs.text:
"waypoints": [ { "id": "WP1", "position": [3000, 1200], "tolerance_m": 40 } ]
Key Unit Default Meaning id text "WP" Name, used in the constraint labels (wp:WP1) position m required [north, east] tolerance_m m 50 The trajectory must pass within this horizontal distance

Waypoints are visited in the order listed. They constrain the horizontal position only, not the altitude, speed or heading. A minimum-fuel optimum usually passes on the edge of the tolerance circle, because going closer costs fuel.

docs.title: Derived quantities
docs.text:
From a mission, the program derives quantities that you do not enter but will see in the results:

Quantity Definition Used for Reference length \(L_{ref}\) Length of the polyline start → waypoints → goal, combined with the altitude change: \(\sqrt{L_h^2+\Delta h^2}\) Scaling of positions, bounds of the flight time, the NFZ margin inflation Reference time \(t_{ref}\) \(L_{ref}/V\) with \(V\) = V_mps Scaling of the flight time and of the cost Planning radius \(R\) \(V^2 / (g\tan(f_b\,\phi_{ws}))\), with \(f_b\) = bank_fraction and \(\phi_{ws}\) = bank_deg Hybrid A* turn radius Altitude band \([\min(h_0,h_f), \max(h_0,h_f)]\) Activity of the no-fly zones

docs.title: 3.4 The pipeline block
docs.text:
"pipeline": {
  "seed": "warm", "stages": "UF>FC", "fc_from_uf": true,
  "nodes_uf": 60, "nodes_fc": 60,
  "alpha": 1.0, "beta_control": 1.0, "beta_state": 1.0,
  "sideslip_max_deg": 1.0, "verify_tol": 1e-4,
  "planner": { "cell_m": 20, "heading_bins": 72, "step_m": 30, "bank_fraction": 0.8, "safety_m": 10 },
  "solver":  { "tol": 1e-6, "acceptable_tol": 1e-4, "max_iter": 1500, "max_cpu_time_s": 120, "print_level": 0 }
}
Key Default Meaning Guidance seed "warm" "warm": Hybrid A* path flown by the guidance laws. "cold": straight line from start to goal Keep "warm". Use "cold" only to measure what the warm start is worth stages "UF>FC" Stages to run: "UF>FC", "UF" or "FC" "UF" is fast and enough for most planning studies; add FC when attitude, rates or surface deflections matter fc_from_uf true Seed the FC stage with the UF optimum. If false, or if the UF stage failed, FC is seeded by the warm start Keep true nodes_uf, nodes_fc 60, 60 Collocation nodes \(N\) of each stage The bundled 3–4 km missions use 60 nodes, one every 50–70 m of path. More nodes resolve turns better and cost more time (section 6.10) alpha 1.0 Cost weight: 0 = minimum time, 1 = minimum fuel, values in between trade one against the other See the tutorial (chapter 5) for the effect beta_control 1.0 Weight of the control-smoothness penalty 1 keeps the penalty at 0–1 % of the cost. Values near 0 give bang-bang thrust beta_state 1.0 Weight of the attitude-smoothness penalty (flight-path angle and bank for UF, roll and pitch for FC) As above sideslip_max_deg 1.0 FC sideslip limit, degrees Keep it small. A large value lets the 6-DoF model use side force as free lift (section 7.4) verify_tol 10⁻⁴ Tolerance of the post-solve verification. Constraint rows are normalised, so this is a relative tolerance Rarely changed planner Hybrid A* settings (below) solver IPOPT settings (below and chapter 8)

docs.title: Planner settings
docs.text:
Key Default Meaning cell_m 20 Size of the search grid cells, metres heading_bins 72 Number of heading cells (72 = 5° each) step_m 30 Length of one motion primitive, metres bank_fraction 0.8 Fraction of bank_deg used to compute the planning radius. The rest is left to the guidance to correct tracking errors safety_m 10 Distance added to every zone margin by the planner

A finer grid (cell_m, heading_bins) finds paths through narrower gaps but expands more search nodes. If the planner finds no path, a smaller safety_m, a finer grid or a larger bank_fraction (tighter planned turns, less bank left for the guidance) usually helps.

docs.title: Solver settings
docs.text:
Key Default Meaning tol 10⁻⁶ Convergence tolerance of IPOPT acceptable_tol 10⁻⁴ Looser tolerance: IPOPT stops with status acceptable if it stays below it for several iterations without reaching tol constr_viol_tol 10⁻⁶ Largest constraint violation accepted at convergence max_iter 1500 Iteration limit max_cpu_time_s 120 Time limit per stage, seconds print_level 0 IPOPT console output: 0 silent, 5 one line per iteration, up to 12 mu_strategy "adaptive" Update rule of the barrier parameter: "adaptive" or "monotone" lbfgs_history 6 Number of correction pairs kept by the limited-memory Hessian approximation linear_solver IPOPT's default Sparse linear solver, for example "mumps", or "ma27"/"ma57" if IPOPT was built with the HSL routines derivative_test false Run IPOPT's first-order derivative checker at the initial point

Chapter 8 explains each option, when to change it and how to read the output.

docs.title: 3.5 Benchmark case files (UC-09)
docs.text:
A UC-09 case file has the same aircraft, pipeline, missions and output keys, plus:

Key Default Meaning pipelines ["COLD>UF", "WS>UF", "WS>FC", "WS>UF>FC"] Pipelines to compare. Each label is a seed (WS = warm start, COLD = straight line) followed by the stages repeats 1 Runs per pipeline and mission; the fastest is kept, to reduce timing noise

Each label overrides seed, stages and fc_from_uf of the pipeline block. All pipelines solve exactly the same problem for a given mission: the scales, the cost references and the bounds of the flight time are computed from the mission, never from the seed.

docs.title: 3.6 The aircraft file
docs.text:
The aircraft file groups the design data. The full list of fields, with units, is in Aircraft file format; the bundled example is data/aircraft/generic_uav.json, an 11 kg UAV with a 2.9 m span.

Group Content Where it enters the optimisation mass Take-off, empty and fuel mass Initial mass; lower bound of the mass geometry Wing area, span, mean chord Aerodynamic forces and moments inertia Body-axis inertia FC rotational dynamics propulsion Sea-level power, propeller efficiency, specific fuel consumption, thrust-line offset Available thrust and power constraint; fuel flow envelope Speeds, minimum altitude, load factors, bank, pitch, flight-path and incidence limits Path constraints of both problems actuators Surface deflection limits, body-rate limits FC control bounds and rate constraints; UF bank-rate constraint aero Lift, drag polar, side force, roll, pitch and yaw derivatives FC uses all of them; UF uses the drag polar and the maximum lift coefficient

The loader stops with a message that names the field when a required value is missing or inconsistent. It checks that:

  • m_empty_kg + fuel_max_kg does not exceed m0_kg, and all masses, lengths and inertias are positive;
  • the inertia tensor is positive definite (\(I_{xx}I_{zz}-I_{xz}^2>0\));
  • eta_p lies in (0, 1];
  • alpha_min_deg < alpha_max_deg, and n_min < 1 < n_max;
  • the lift slope and the induced-drag factor are positive, and \(C_L\) at alpha_max_deg is positive;
  • \(C_{m\alpha}<0\) (static stability in pitch);
  • the stall speed at sea level is below V_ne.

Quantities such as the maximum lift coefficient, the stall speed at each altitude and mass, the available thrust and the best lift-to-drag speed are always derived from these data, never entered.

Checking a new aircraft. Point the case files of UC-01 and UC-05 at the new file and run them before any optimisation. UC-01 prints the derived performance; UC-05 draws the power curves, the flight envelope and the trim curves, which reveal unrealistic coefficients quickly (for example an elevator that cannot trim the aircraft at cruise speed).

docs.title: 3.7 Checklist before running a new case
docs.text:
1. The end position and both headings describe the mission you intend: north first, east second; heading clockwise from north.
  2. Every zone polygon is simple and its altitude band is the one you mean. A zone below the whole flight is ignored.
  3. Waypoints are listed in visiting order, and each tolerance is reachable with the aircraft's turn radius.
  4. The start and goal are outside every active zone plus its margin.
  5. V_mps lies between the stall speed and V_ne at h0_m (UC-01 prints both).
  6. nodes_uf and nodes_fc are large enough for the path length (section 6.10).
  7. The output folder is new, or you do not mind overwriting its contents.

docs.title: 4. Reading the results
docs.text: A UC-08 run reports its results three times: as a table on the console, as CSV files with every trajectory, and as a JSON report with the status of every stage. This chapter explains each of them and ends with a checklist for deciding whether a run can be trusted.

docs.title: 4.1 The console table
docs.text:
./build/ofc data/cases/uc08_optimal_missions.json prints one row per mission (Windows laptop, IPOPT 3.14.20):

== UC-08  Optimal missions (warm start -> UF -> FC, IPOPT) ==
pipeline WS>UF>FC, N = 60 (UF) / 60 (FC), alpha = 1.00 (0 time, 1 fuel), beta = 1.00 (controls) / 1.00 (attitude)

id     | WS[ms] | UF           it   t[ms]  tf[s] fuel_g pen% | FC           it   t[ms]  tf[s] fuel_g pen% | clrUF clrFC  wpUF  wpFC  simUF
M-01   |    221 | solved      100     479  152.3    6.2    1 | solved       89     653  152.5    6.2    1 |     9     9     -     -   0.34
M-02   |    505 | solved      106     552  178.4    7.4    1 | acceptable   87    1046  178.7    7.4    1 |    11    11     -     -   0.38
M-03   |    182 | solved       96    1622  199.1    8.3    1 | solved       99    2902  199.2    8.3    1 |     -     -  40.0  40.0   0.89
M-04   |   1510 | solved      145    3699  185.8   11.5    0 | solved       98    3086  186.6   11.5    0 |    12    12  35.2  35.3   0.62

The header line repeats the settings actually used: the pipeline label, the node counts and the cost weights. Check it first; a misspelt key in the case file shows up here as a default value.

Column Meaning Good value id Mission identifier WS[ms] Time of the warm start: Hybrid A* search plus both guidance runs Small compared with the solves UF, FC Final status of each stage (section 4.2); - if the stage did not run solved or acceptable, without ! it IPOPT iterations of the stage t[ms] Wall-clock time of the IPOPT call Machine-dependent tf[s] Optimal flight time fuel_g Fuel burnt, grams: initial minus final mass pen% Share of the final cost due to the smoothness penalties A few percent at most clrUF, clrFC Smallest horizontal distance beyond any active zone's margin, measured along the straight segments between nodes, metres. - if no zone is active ≥ 0 wpUF, wpFC Largest horizontal distance between a waypoint and the trajectory, metres. - without waypoints ≤ the waypoint's tolerance simUF Largest position error of an RK4 simulation of each interval, started from its node and driven by the optimal UF controls, metres Small compared with the node spacing

simUF measures the discretisation error of the collocation: the difference between what the collocated model predicts over one interval and what an accurate integration of the same controls gives. It is restarted at every node, so it does not grow with the flight length. (summary.csv also contains sim_drift_uf_m, a single open-loop simulation over the whole flight, which drifts by tens of metres because small heading and speed errors integrate; a tracking controller removes that drift in flight.)

docs.title: 4.2 Stage status
docs.text:
Status Meaning Counts as converged solved IPOPT reached its tolerance tol ✓ acceptable IPOPT reached the looser acceptable_tol for several consecutive iterations without reaching tol ✓ infeasible IPOPT converged to a point that minimises the constraint violation but does not satisfy the constraints max_iter The iteration limit max_iter was reached max_time The time limit max_cpu_time_s was reached failed Any other IPOPT outcome: restoration failure, step too small, invalid numbers, and so on no_solver The program was built without IPOPT

A stage is successful only if IPOPT converged and the independent verification (section 4.3) found no violated constraint or bound. A stage that is not successful is marked with a trailing ! (for example max_iter!, or solved! if IPOPT converged but the verification failed; a failed stage is shown without it), the row ends with (CHECK), and one line per failed stage follows with IPOPT's return code and the verification summary. With max_iter reduced to 20, for example:

T-03   |     53 | max_iter!    20     130  179.9   10.1    1 | max_iter!    20     158  183.5   10.2    1 |    22    22  41.5  39.0   0.93  (CHECK)
       UF: Maximum_Iterations_Exceeded; dynamics 179 (defect gamma @56 2.7e-02) | boundary ok | envelope ok | environment 1 (wp:WP1 @38 8.0e-02) | bounds ok
       FC: Maximum_Iterations_Exceeded; dynamics 1 (defect p @53 1.5e-04) | boundary ok | envelope ok | environment ok | bounds ok

If the warm start itself fails (no path found, or the guidance did not reach the goal), a line warm start: <reason> is printed, and the UF stage falls back to a straight-line initial point.

docs.title: 4.3 The verification report
docs.text:
After each solve, nlp::verify evaluates every constraint and every variable bound at the final point, outside IPOPT, and groups the violations larger than verify_tol (default 10⁻⁴) by kind:

Group Rows Example label dynamics Collocation defects: the equations of motion between consecutive nodes defect gamma @56: flight-path-angle equation, interval 56 boundary Initial state and final position and heading x0.V, xf.chi envelope Path constraints from the aircraft envelope stall @12, power @30, sideslip @7 environment No-fly zones and waypoints nfz:A @41, wp:WP1 @38 bounds Box bounds of the variables, relative to the variable's scale V @3, tf

@k is the node (or, for defects, the interval starting at node k), counted from 0. For each group the report gives the number of violations, the worst one and its label, for example dynamics 179 (defect gamma @56 2.7e-02). All rows are normalised (chapter 7), so a value of 2.7·10⁻² means a violation of 2.7 % of the row's reference scale.

The verification exists because a solver's own convergence test is made on its internally scaled problem; re-evaluating the original rows confirms that the optimum satisfies what the case file asked for.

docs.title: 4.4 Output files of UC-08
docs.text: All files are written to the folder given by output. Numbers have ten significant digits.

docs.title: Per mission
docs.text:
File Rows Columns <id>_ws.csv Warm start, resampled on the UF nodes (the initial point of the UF stage) as <id>_uf.csv <id>_uf.csv Point-mass optimum, one row per node t, x, y, h, V, gamma_deg, chi_deg, bank_deg, m, T, CL, p_dps <id>_fc.csv 6-DoF optimum, one row per node t, x, y, h, Va, alpha_deg, beta_deg, phi_deg, theta_deg, psi_deg, p_dps, q_dps, r_dps, m, T, de_deg, da_deg, dr_deg <id>_path.csv Hybrid A* path, sampled every 5 m x, y, psi_deg <id>_nfz.csv Vertices of every zone zone (index), x, y, h_min, h_max, margin, active (1 or 0) <id>_points.csv Start, waypoints and goal x, y, tolerance; the start has tolerance -1 and the goal -2

Column symbols: x north and y east position [m], h altitude [m], V/Va airspeed [m/s], gamma flight-path angle, chi heading, bank/phi bank (roll) angle, theta pitch, psi yaw, alpha incidence, beta sideslip, m mass [kg], T thrust [N], CL lift coefficient, p UF bank rate or FC roll rate, q pitch rate, r yaw rate, de/da/dr elevator, aileron and rudder deflections. Angles are in degrees and rates in degrees per second.

The controls at the last node of a trajectory are decision variables like any other, but they only act through the final half interval, so they are less meaningful than the others.

docs.title: Per case
docs.text:
summary.csv has one row per mission, with the console values at full precision plus a few more:

Column Meaning index Position of the mission in the case file ws_ms Warm-start time uf_ok, fc_ok 1 if the stage succeeded (converged and verified), else 0 uf_iter, uf_ms, fc_iter, fc_ms Iterations and solve times tf_uf, tf_fc, fuel_uf_g, fuel_fc_g Flight time and fuel of each optimum clearance_uf_m, clearance_fc_m As clrUF, clrFC; nan without active zones wp_miss_uf_m, wp_miss_fc_m As wpUF, wpFC; 0 without waypoints sim_local_uf_m, sim_drift_uf_m Interval-restarted and whole-flight simulation errors (section 4.1) guess_defect_uf, guess_defect_fc Largest normalised collocation defect of each stage's initial point: how far the seed is from satisfying the dynamics penalty_uf_pct, penalty_fc_pct As pen%

report.json holds one record per mission:

{
  "id": "T-01", "title": "Empty airspace", "pipeline": "WS>UF>FC", "total_ms": 1319.4,
  "warm_start": { "ran": true, "ok": true, "status": "ok", "message": "ok", "millis": 36.0, ... },
  "uf": {
    "ran": true, "ok": true, "status": "solved", "message": "Solve_Succeeded",
    "seed": "warm start (UF guidance run)",
    "millis": 539.4, "iterations": 116, "objective": 0.37027,
    "guess_defect": 0.215, "penalty_share": 0.0065,
    "verification": "dynamics ok | boundary ok | envelope ok | environment ok | bounds ok"
  },
  "fc": { ..., "seed": "UF optimum (projected)", ... }
}

seed records where the stage's initial point came from (sections 6.5 and 6.7). message is IPOPT's own return code (chapter 8). objective is the final value of the cost function (chapter 7); penalty_share is the fraction of it due to the smoothness terms.

docs.title: 4.5 Output files of UC-09
docs.text:
UC-09 prints one row per mission and pipeline:

id     pipeline   | WS[ms] | UF           it   t[ms] | FC           it   t[ms] |    total       J  tf[s] fuel_g
M-04   COLD>UF    |      0 | solved      124     625  | -                        |      626  0.6106  195.3  11.96
M-04   WS>UF      |    286 | solved      103     512  | -                        |      798  0.5877  185.8  11.55

total is the wall-clock time of the whole pipeline, and J, tf[s] and fuel_g describe the result of its last stage. With repeats > 1 the fastest repetition is reported. The same data are in benchmark.csv (stage flags are -1 when a stage did not run) and, with the full stage records of section 4.4, in benchmark.json.

docs.title: 4.6 Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 Every case ran and every check passed. Also returned when UC-08 or UC-09 are skipped because IPOPT is missing 1 No case file given, or a case stopped with an error (file not found, invalid JSON, missing key, invalid aircraft). The message is printed as error (<file>): <reason> 2 A case ran, but at least one mission did not pass its checks: a UC-08 stage did not succeed, or a UC-07 path was not found or violated a zone or waypoint

UC-09 returns 0 even when some pipelines fail, because a failed pipeline is a legitimate benchmark result. Scripts that run cases unattended should test the exit code.

docs.title: 4.7 Figures
docs.text:
python utils/plot_results.py (or --optimal <folder> for your own case) draws, for UC-08:

  • uc08_cover.png: top view of every mission, with the Hybrid A* path (thin black), the flown warm start (grey dash-dot), the UF optimum (blue), the FC optimum (red dashed), the active zones with their margin (dotted) and the waypoints with their tolerance circle;
  • uc08_<id>.png: the same top view next to altitude, airspeed, bank and thrust against time, for the warm start and both optima.

Zones below the flight are drawn hatched in grey: they are inactive and may be overflown.

docs.title: 4.8 Is the result trustworthy?
docs.text:
Go through these checks in order:

  1. Status. Every stage is solved or acceptable, without !, and the row has no (CHECK).
  2. Clearance and waypoints. clr ≥ 0 and wp within the tolerance. Both are measured between nodes as well, so they are stricter than the constraints the solver saw.
  3. Discretisation error. simUF is a small fraction of the node spacing (path length divided by N − 1). If it is not, increase the number of nodes.
  4. Penalty share. pen% stays at a few percent. A large share means the smoothness terms, not the mission, shape the optimum; reduce beta_control and beta_state.
  5. Model agreement. UF and FC flight time and fuel agree closely (within about 1 % in the bundled missions). A large gap points to a seed problem or to the sideslip limit (section 7.4).
  6. Physics. The profiles make sense: for minimum fuel the airspeed settles near the best lift-to-drag speed (UC-01 prints it), turns use moderate bank, and thrust is smooth.

IPOPT finds local optima. Two different seeds can converge to two different optima of the same problem, as UC-09 shows for mission M-04 (cold start: 195 s and 11.96 g; warm start: 186 s and 11.55 g). The warm start makes a good local optimum likely, not certain.

docs.title: 5. Tutorial: your first mission
docs.text:
This tutorial builds a mission in three steps, runs the full optimisation on each one, and then changes the cost to see how the optimum responds. Every number below was produced with data/cases/tutorial_first_mission.json on a Windows laptop with IPOPT 3.14.20; your iteration counts and times will differ slightly.

The task. The generic UAV of the repository flies at 300 m and 25 m/s, heading north from the origin. It must reach a point 3 km north and 1 km east, arriving on an easterly heading. We first solve it in empty airspace, then add a no-fly zone on the direct route, then add a waypoint and a 100 m climb.

docs.title: 5.1 Step 1: empty airspace (T-01)
docs.text:
The case file starts with the use case, the aircraft and the pipeline settings. The values below are the defaults written out in full, so that every setting is visible:

"use_case": "UC-08",
"aircraft": "data/aircraft/generic_uav.json",
"pipeline": {
  "seed": "warm", "stages": "UF>FC",
  "nodes_uf": 60, "nodes_fc": 60,
  "alpha": 1.0, "beta_control": 1.0, "beta_state": 1.0, "sideslip_max_deg": 1.0,
  "planner": { "cell_m": 20, "heading_bins": 72, "step_m": 30, "bank_fraction": 0.8, "safety_m": 10 },
  "solver": { "tol": 1e-6, "acceptable_tol": 1e-4, "max_iter": 1500, "max_cpu_time_s": 120, "print_level": 0 }
},

In words: seed the optimisation with the warm start, solve the point-mass problem and then the 6-DoF problem on 60 nodes each, minimise fuel (alpha = 1) with the standard smoothness penalties, and keep the 6-DoF model in coordinated flight.

The first mission only states the start and the goal:

{
  "id": "T-01", "title": "Empty airspace",
  "h0_m": 300, "climb_m": 0, "V_mps": 25, "bank_deg": 30,
  "start": [0, 0], "start_heading_deg": 0, "end": [3000, 1000], "end_heading_deg": 90
}

bank_deg sets the turn radius of the warm start: \(R = V^2/(g\tan(0.8\cdot 30°)) = 143\) m. It does not limit the optimiser, which may bank up to the aircraft's phi_max_deg (40°).

docs.title: 5.2 Step 2: a no-fly zone on the direct route (T-02)
docs.text:
T-02 is T-01 with one zone added. The square covers north 1200 to 1900 m and east -200 to 700 m, from the ground to 1000 m, with a 40 m margin. The straight line from the start to the goal passes through it.

"nfz": [
  { "id": "Z1", "polygon": [[1200, -200], [1900, -200], [1900, 700], [1200, 700]],
    "h_min_m": 0, "h_max_m": 1000, "margin_m": 40 }
]

docs.title: 5.3 Step 3: a waypoint and a climb (T-03)
docs.text:
T-03 keeps the zone, asks the aircraft to pass within 40 m of a point west of it, and to arrive 100 m higher:

"climb_m": 100,
"waypoints": [ { "id": "WP1", "position": [2400, -300], "tolerance_m": 40 } ]

docs.title: 5.4 Run
docs.text:
./build/ofc data/cases/tutorial_first_mission.json

id     | WS[ms] | UF           it   t[ms]  tf[s] fuel_g pen% | FC           it   t[ms]  tf[s] fuel_g pen% | clrUF clrFC  wpUF  wpFC  simUF
T-01   |     36 | solved      116     539  152.1    6.2    1 | solved      113     743  152.4    6.2    1 |     -     -     -     -   0.72
T-02   |    171 | solved       99     509  156.9    6.4    1 | solved      116     964  157.5    6.5    1 |     9     9     -     -   1.00
T-03   |    162 | solved      106    2331  183.2   10.1    1 | solved      122    3726  183.6   10.1    1 |    23    22  39.1  39.1   0.48

Go through the checklist of section 4.8:

  1. All six stages are solved, none is marked with !, so every stage converged and passed the verification.
  2. The optimal paths keep 9 m (T-02) and 22–23 m (T-03) beyond the 40 m margin, measured along the segments between nodes. In T-03 the waypoint is passed 39.1 m from its centre, inside the 40 m tolerance.
  3. simUF is under 1 m, against a node spacing of about 55–65 m.
  4. The smoothness penalties are about 1 % of the cost.
  5. The point-mass and 6-DoF optima agree to 0.4 % in flight time and to 0.1 g in fuel.

docs.title: 5.5 Plot
docs.text:
python utils/plot_results.py --optimal output/tutorial

The figures are written to output/figures/tutorial_cover.png and tutorial_T-01.png to tutorial_T-03.png.

Black: Hybrid A* path. Grey dash-dot: warm start flown by the guidance. Blue: point-mass (UF) optimum. Red dashed: 6-DoF (FC) optimum. Red square: the no-fly zone, with its margin dotted. Green diamond: the waypoint with its tolerance circle.

docs.title: 5.6 Interpretation
docs.text:
T-01. With nothing in the way, the optimum is almost a straight line followed by a turn onto the final heading. The path is 3.20 km long against 3.16 km for the straight line between the end points, because the aircraft must turn from north to east. The flight takes 152 s, so the mean ground speed is about 21 m/s, not the 25 m/s the aircraft started with: to minimise fuel it slows down to about 21 m/s, its best lift-to-drag speed (20.8 m/s at sea level, UC-01), and stays there.

T-02. The zone forces a detour round its east side. The optimum hugs the corner of the margin more closely than the warm start, which kept the planner's extra 10 m of safety distance. The detour costs 4.8 s and 0.2 g of fuel (3 %).

T-03. The waypoint lies west of the zone, so the path now passes on the west side and then turns north-east to the goal.

The profiles show the difference between a flyable trajectory and an optimal one:

  • Altitude. The warm start climbs the 100 m at once, at its commanded 7.5° climb angle, then cruises. Both optima instead stay low at first and spread the climb over the whole flight.
  • Airspeed. The warm start holds 25 m/s. The optima slow to about 20.5 m/s, and in the last seconds bleed speed down to about 15 m/s, close to the stall speed, because the final speed is free and kinetic energy left at the goal would be fuel wasted.
  • Thrust. The warm start needs 23 N during its climb, near the power limit. The optima use a smooth thrust profile that never exceeds 15 N.
  • Fuel. T-03 burns 10.1 g against 6.4 g for T-02. Most of the difference is the potential energy of the climb: \(mg\Delta h\) = 11 kg × 9.81 m/s² × 100 m = 10.8 kJ, which at the aircraft's propeller efficiency (0.7) and specific fuel consumption (0.6 kg/kWh) costs 2.6 g. The longer path (183 s against 157 s) accounts for the rest.

The two models time the climb differently (the 6-DoF optimum first descends about 15 m before climbing) but burn the same fuel: for this propulsion model, the fuel cost of a climb hardly depends on when it is flown.

docs.title: 5.7 Change the objective
docs.text:
Edit "alpha" in the pipeline block and run again. alpha = 0 minimises flight time, 1 minimises fuel, and 0.5 weighs both (each term is normalised by its own reference, so the weights are comparable; section 7.7). Point-mass results:

Mission α = 1 (fuel) α = 0.5 α = 0 (time) T-01 152.1 s, 6.2 g 101.1 s, 8.7 g 87.7 s, 11.4 g T-02 156.9 s, 6.4 g 104.1 s, 9.0 g 90.4 s, 11.7 g T-03 183.2 s, 10.1 g 121.8 s, 13.2 g 113.7 s, 14.6 g

Minimum time cuts the flight time by 40 % and nearly doubles the fuel. The minimum-time T-01 also shows how the optimiser uses every freedom it has:

  • It accelerates from 25 m/s to 39 m/s, just below the never-exceed speed of 40 m/s, in a shallow dive. At that speed the thrust (14 N) is limited by the available power, so the power constraint is active.
  • It descends about 70 m below the start altitude to gain speed, and zooms back up to the required final altitude in the last 15 seconds, trading kinetic energy for height while it banks 35° onto the final heading. The minimum-time UF solves also needed fewer iterations here: 35 to 39, against 99 to 116 for minimum fuel.

The intermediate value α = 0.5 gives about four fifths of the time saving for about half of the extra fuel, which is the kind of trade-off the weight is for.

docs.title: 5.8 Exercises
docs.text:
Each of these changes one setting of a copy of the tutorial file; compare the console table with the one in section 5.4. The outcomes quoted were obtained on the same machine.

  1. Point mass only. Set "stages": "UF". The UF columns are unchanged and the FC columns show -. The run is much faster, and for planning studies the point-mass optimum is usually enough.
  2. Cold start. Set "seed": "cold". The UF stage now starts from a straight line through the zone. T-01 and T-02 still reach the same optima, with more iterations for T-02 (128 against 99). T-03 converges to a different, worse local optimum: 229 s and 12.1 g instead of 183 s and 10.1 g. This is the situation the warm start exists to avoid (section 6.1).
  3. Watch IPOPT. Set "print_level": 5 in the solver block and run T-02 alone (delete the other missions from your copy). Chapter 8 explains every column of the log.
  4. Number of nodes. Set "nodes_uf": 25. The UF solves become several times faster, but simUF grows from under 1 m to 4–7 m, and the clearance grows to 47–70 m because the zone margin is inflated more to protect the longer segments between nodes (section 7.5). With "nodes_uf": 120, simUF drops to 0.1–0.2 m, the clearance shrinks to 3–6 m and the optimum improves slightly (151.5 s instead of 152.1 s for T-01), at a higher cost per iteration.
  5. A tighter waypoint. Reduce tolerance_m of WP1 to 10 m and observe the extra time and fuel needed to pass closer.
  6. A second zone. Add a zone between the start and WP1 and check that both clearances stay positive.

Save your changes in a new file such as data/cases/my_mission.json, not in the bundled ones. Avoid the uc0 prefix, so that run.sh keeps running only the bundled cases.
